feature_under_test: MySQL TCP connections are forcibly closed and temporarily refused while a real-Chrome request is in flight

environment.mysql: ephemeral MySQL 8.4 with separate non-root migration and runtime accounts
environment.fault_proxy: test-process transparent TCP proxy between all Recruiting runtime clients and MySQL

fault_cut.browser_state_before_cut: Attempt running, no Artifact persisted, and controlled origin accepted exactly one document request
fault_cut.cut: close every existing proxied MySQL TCP connection, refuse new connections for seven seconds, then resume forwarding to the same database

first_run_finding.facts: the website was requested once, but the original Attempt and Work remained running with zero Artifacts and the originating dispatch waited on its fifteen-minute acknowledgement deadline
first_run_finding.root_cause: the Executor retried only ambiguous Call/Wait transport outcomes; the control Actor's explicit internal_unavailable response after a database connection reset was treated as terminal, so the already-produced immutable result was abandoned
first_run_finding.fix_scope: Recruiting Executor control client only: replay the identical result operation and payload on internal_unavailable or channel_unavailable with bounded exponential backoff; business rejection and protocol errors remain terminal

invariants: all Recruiting runtime database traffic uses the non-root staircase_runtime account through the fault proxy
the fault closes established TCP connections and rejects new connections only after the Attempt is running, the request reached the origin, and no Artifact exists
the result command ID, result operation, Attempt identity, Executor incarnation and payload remain byte-stable across retries
temporary internal_unavailable and channel_unavailable responses use bounded exponential backoff; business rejection and protocol errors are never retried
the original Attempt succeeds without a replacement Attempt, recovery dispatch, or second website request
single-result and batch-result control clients share the same retry rule
all Permits and dispatches settle, and final Server restart preserves the completed state and both Resources

implementation.retry_policy: immediate single replay for ambiguous delivery; 250ms exponential backoff capped at 2s for explicit internal_unavailable/channel_unavailable, bounded by control_wait_ms

non_claims: MySQL primary/replica failover, data loss, or transaction recovery after database process death
remote-network latency, packet reordering, partial packet corruption, or a long outage beyond control_wait_ms
simultaneous Atoll Server and MySQL failure
remote Artifact storage or third-party site availability

acceptance.gate: P9 MySQL connection reset during an in-flight real-Chrome request
